transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since the wreck two weeks ago, I just can’t think straight long enough to do my work or make simple decisions, it’s like my mind keeps stalling out. My wife pushed me to get help because it is severely affecting my ability to manage my tax business and handle things at home.
Did you lose consciousness, experience a head injury, or have any memory gaps immediately following the car accident?

The ER doctors said I didn't have any head injuries, just some minor bumps and scrapes, but I definitely have a major memory gap. I remember seeing the headlights coming at me and the truck spinning, but after that, there's just a big empty hole until I was suddenly outside on a stretcher. No matter how hard I try, I can't fill in those minutes in between.
Do you find yourself having unwanted, vivid memories of the crash or feeling like you are reliving the accident when you are awake?

No, I don't really experience those kinds of flashbacks or feel like I'm reliving the crash during the day. While I can picture the truck spinning when I think back on it, I'm not having those vivid, unwanted memories popping up out of nowhere while I'm awake.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any neurological conditions, or have you noticed any other physical symptoms like seizures or unusual headaches since the accident?

No, I have never been diagnosed with any neurological conditions, and I haven't experienced any seizures or unusual headaches since the accident. The doctors at the ER checked me over and said I only had minor physical injuries, so physically I've been okay.
Since the accident, have you noticed your memory gaps or difficulty thinking clearly getting worse when you are under stress or discussing the crash, or is this a constant, persistent state?

The memory gap is a constant, specific blank spot—that chunk of time between seeing the headlights and waking up on the stretcher is just completely gone all the time. As for the difficulty thinking, it has been a constant, persistent struggle ever since the accident, especially whenever I sit down to work or try to make simple decisions.
Do you feel like you are observing yourself from outside your body, or that the world around you feels unreal or dreamlike since the accident?

Yes, especially when I'm riding in a car or passing the intersection where it happened. Everything suddenly feels weirdly far away and fake, almost like I'm watching a movie of my own life. It feels like I'm not really inside my own body, but just floating a few feet behind myself.
Since the accident, have you ever felt like you have different parts of your personality that take control at different times, or have you discovered items or notes you don't remember acquiring?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I've never felt like different parts of my personality were taking over, and I haven't found any items or notes that I don't remember getting.
Have these feelings of being detached from your body and the difficulty with your thinking been present consistently every day since the accident, or do they come and go in waves?

The difficulty with my thinking has been constant every single day since the accident, especially when I try to work. On the other hand, the feeling of being detached from my body comes in waves, mostly when I'm riding in a car or near that intersection. Both of these issues started right after the wreck two weeks ago.
Since the accident, have you been experiencing significant sadness, anxiety, or a sense of being overwhelmed that feels like a struggle to adjust to the life changes caused by the crash?

Yes, I feel incredibly anxious and overwhelmed, and I'm constantly on edge scanning for danger. Even simple daily decisions like picking which email to answer first feel impossible, making it very hard to adjust to these changes. It has gotten to the point where my wife has had to take over my responsibilities, like paying the bills, because I just can't keep up.

Do you feel that your current difficulty with thinking and detachment is primarily a reaction to the stress of the accident and the life changes it caused, or does it feel like a separate, involuntary 'shutting down' of your identity or memory that is independent of your emotional distress?

While it all absolutely started with the wreck, this feels like an involuntary, automatic shutting down rather than just normal stress. The memory gap, my mind blanking out at work, and those weird out-of-body feelings make me feel like my brain is stalling or disconnecting on its own, completely out of my control.

Since the accident, have you experienced any periods where you felt like you had lost your sense of identity or felt like a completely different person, or are these dissociative feelings strictly limited to the memory gap and the sensation of being detached from your physical body?

No, I haven't lost my sense of identity or felt like a different person at all. These feelings are strictly limited to that blank spot in my memory from the crash and those moments where I feel detached from my physical body, like I'm watching myself from behind. I still know exactly who I am, it's just that my brain and body feel disconnected in those moments.

When you experience these periods of detachment, does the world around you feel completely unreal or dreamlike, and do you find it difficult to recall personal information other than the specific memories of the accident?

Yes, during those moments of detachment—especially when I'm in a car or near that intersection—everything around me feels fake, far away, and like I'm watching a movie. But I don't have any trouble remembering my general personal information; it is really just that one frustrating blank spot in my memory covering those few minutes of the crash.
Beyond the specific memory gap of the crash, do you find that you frequently experience these 'dreamlike' or 'out-of-body' sensations in situations unrelated to the accident or reminders of it?

No, they don't happen randomly in completely unrelated situations. Those dreamlike, out-of-body feelings are strictly tied to reminders of the accident, like when I'm riding in a car or walking past that intersection. In those moments, I feel like I'm watching my life like a movie and floating behind myself, but it doesn't just pop up out of nowhere.

Since the accident, have you been experiencing persistent symptoms like difficulty sleeping, being easily startled, or feeling constantly on edge, even when you are not near the intersection or reminded of the crash?

Yes, I am constantly on edge and easily startled, even just sitting at home where I find myself checking the windows and scanning for exits. If a car door slams outside or my wife walks into my office without me hearing her first, I jerk so hard I almost come out of my chair with my heart racing. It takes a really long time to calm back down.

Do you find that your primary distress is centered around these dissociative 'shutting down' experiences, or is it the persistent anxiety, startle response, and inability to function that bothers you the most?

While both are highly distressing, the inability to think clearly and do my work is definitely the most stressful part because it is threatening my livelihood and forcing my wife to take over my responsibilities. The constant jumpiness and those weird out-of-body feelings are terrifying, but the practical impact of not being able to manage my daily life is what is causing the most distress.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits classic symptoms of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder following a severe accident, including persistent hyperarousal (startle response, being on edge), dissociative symptoms (depersonalization and derealization tied to trauma reminders), and significant functional impairment. While the memory gap is present, it is consistent with trauma-related dissociative amnesia rather than a primary dissociative identity disorder.
